name: Kettlebell Deep Squat to Overhead Press
description: Bell racked on one side. Sink into a full, deep squat — heels down, hips below the knees — and hold the bottom for a beat with the rack tight and the free arm reaching forward for balance. Stand all the way up, and only then press the bell overhead. The leg drive does NOT feed the press the way a thruster's does: you finish the squat first and the press is strict, so the bell covers the longest path a press can cover. Slower and more honest than a thruster at the same load — the deep bottom position is where it gets hard, and the strict press at the end has no momentum to hide behind. Also loosely called a 'long press' (Madeleine Conti's label; the name is about the long path, not a distinct technique). Can be run from a kickstand (staggered) stance for extra single-arm stability.
